newsitem.title: SOUTH KOREA: Seoul stocks close up, foreign ownership raised.
newsitem.headline: Seoul stocks close up, foreign ownership raised.

text.p: South Korean stocks closed higher on Monday on an imminent announcement of raising foreign stock ownership ceiling, brokers said.
The composite index closed 1.52 percent, or 10.15 points, higher at 677.34.
After the market closed, the finance and economy ministry announced a three percentage-point increase in the ceiling to 23 percent, effective from May 1.
"People believed the announcement was imminent. They actively bought shares, which are foreigners' favourites," said Shim Choong-bo, research manager of Daishin Securities.

Analysts said although some blue chips would attract strong buying in reaction to the announcement, the impact would be short-lived. They said Samsung Electronics, SK Telecom, Pohang Iron and Steel, Kookmin Bank and Shinhan Bank would benefit most from the increased ceiling.

"Most of the rebound we saw in the past couple of days reflected the expected increase in foreign investment limit," said Namuh Rhee, head of research at Dongbang Peregrine Securities. "Therefore, I think the actual announcement will have limited impact on stock market.
Samsung Electronics rose by 700 won to 59,900, SK Telecom by 30,000 won to 495,000, Kookmin Bank by 300 won to 12,300 and Shinhan Bank by 400 won to 10,700.

Miwon Petrochemical rose 640 won to its daily limit of 6,450 on Korea Kumho Petrochemical's announcement that it had agreed to buy the biggest single stake of 25.1 percent in Miwon over-the-counter. Korea Kumho closed 10 won higher at 6,360.
Daesung Industrial lost 500 won to 49,400 after it announced a plan to absorb its affiliate Daesung Resources. Daesung Resources also fell 100 won to 84,600.
